exact_claim.theorem: There exist absolute C,kappa>0,H0 such that for each fixed integer H>=H0, all sufficiently large x, simultaneously every real 0<=t<=x, K(t)/(x G_m/log x)<=C exp(-kappa B/m^4)+C sum_{h>=H} h^4 exp(-kappa rho^(-h)/h^3).
exact_claim.requested_source_consequence: For fixed c>1, t=x or x/c, K(t)<=(epsilon_H+o_{x;H}(1))x G_m/log x, epsilon_H->0 uniformly in phase.
exact_claim.objects: K counts ordered unequal good prefix-tail tuple pairs with equal F=d product(p_j-1), not values, witnesses or tail preimages.
exact_claim.all_endpoint_extension: The original source's two-endpoint definition is extended by the same fixed-x tuple predicate and closed F<=t restriction; no parameters are recomputed from t.

exact_hypotheses: Natural logarithms; rho is the unique defining root in (0,1), and the root bracket is independently proved.
H is a fixed sufficiently large positive integer, chosen before x tends to infinity; the estimates are uniform over all H<=h<=m and all phases.
All scales, prime bands, simplex constraints, cut indices, S-normality thresholds and residual thresholds are formed from x.
Every basic witness of a good tuple satisfies the conditions at every comparison index; tail witness multiplicity is not tuple multiplicity.
Residuals are positive, repeated prime factors are retained, and both residual factorizations are counted.
The whole displayed comparison product is squarefree on primes strictly above z; Ford's last cutoff is strictly larger than z.
Ford is applied with k=b, ell=1, f_1=1, including b=1, and with all its original restrictions plus k<=log_2 y.
The same value function and closed endpoint predicate are retained at all t.
